title: Margin vs padding
summary: You know both add space. Learn which side of the border each one lives on, and when vertical margins collapse.
objective: Pick margin or padding for any spacing job, and predict the gap when vertical margins meet.

hook.prompt: This small text button is hard to tap. A teammate adds `margin: 12px` to it. What changes?

visual.alt: A tiny secondary button labelled Undo, with its label close to its edges.
visual.html: Message deleted.

options.text: The tappable area grows by 12px on every side
options.feedback: Margin sits outside the button, so the extra space isn't part of what you tap.

options.text: The button stays the same size; only its neighbours move further away
The label gets 12px of room inside the button
options.feedback: Room inside the button's background is a different property. Margin goes outside the edge.

hook.explanation: Margin adds space outside the button that isn't part of it, so the tap target stays just as small. The fix lives inside the border.

bricks.title: Inside the border or outside it
bricks.body: Both add space, on opposite sides of the **border**. **Padding** sits inside: it's painted with the element's background, it counts as part of the box, and people can click or tap it. **Margin** sits outside: it's always transparent, never clickable, and only pushes neighbours away. So ask: should this space *belong to* the element, or sit *between* elements?

visual.alt: Box model diagram: a dashed transparent margin ring outside a solid border, a tinted padding area inside the border, and the content in the middle.
visual.html:
margin (transparent)
padding (painted, clickable)border
content

bricks.prompt: Which property fits each spacing job?

items.text: Room between a button's label and its edge
A bigger tap target for a small icon button
Tinted space around the text in a banner
A gap between two stacked cards
Pushing a footer away from the content above it
Clear space around a logo that other elements must keep out of

bricks.explanation: Space that should look or feel like part of the element (tinted, tappable) is padding. Space that only keeps other elements away is margin.

bricks.prompt: A white card with a 1px border sits on a grey page. You change its `padding: 16px` to `margin: 16px`. What does the user see?

options.text: The text now touches the border, and grey page shows in a 16px ring around the card
Nothing; the same 16px of space just moved
options.feedback: The space moved across the border. It was white and inside the card; now it's outside, where the page shows through.

options.text: The white area grows by 16px on each side
options.feedback: That's what adding padding does. Margin is transparent, so it shows the grey page, not the card's white.

bricks.hint: Which side of the border is each property on?
bricks.explanation: Padding was the white space inside the border. As margin, it moves outside and turns transparent, so the text meets the border and grey shows around the card.

bricks.title: The catch: vertical margins collapse
bricks.body: When two vertical margins touch in normal block flow, the browser keeps only the **larger** one. A heading with `margin-bottom: 24px` above a paragraph with `margin-top: 16px` leaves a 24px gap, not 40px. A first child's top margin can also slip out through a parent with no top padding or border, landing above the parent's background. Padding never collapses, and neither do horizontal margins or the margins of flex and grid items.

term.definition: When touching vertical margins merge into one, the size of the larger.

visual.alt: A heading block with a 24px bottom margin above a paragraph block with a 16px top margin; the gap between them is labelled 24px, not 40px.
visual.html:
h2 margin-bottom: 24px
gap: 24px, not 40px
p margin-top: 16px

bricks.prompt: Two cards stack in normal block flow. The upper card has `margin-bottom: 32px`; the lower card has `margin-top: 20px`. How much space separates them?

options.feedback: That adds them up. Touching vertical margins in block flow collapse instead of stacking.
Right idea, wrong margin: the larger one wins, not the smaller.
The browser doesn't subtract one margin from the other; it keeps the larger one whole.

bricks.hint: Do these margins add up, or does one of them win?
bricks.explanation: The two vertical margins touch in normal flow, so they collapse to the larger one: 32px.

bricks.prompt: Which of these collapse into a single margin?

options.text: A heading's `margin-bottom` and the next paragraph's `margin-top`, in normal block flow
A first child's `margin-top` and the top of a parent that has no padding or border
Two stacked cards' vertical margins inside a `display: grid` container
options.feedback: Grid items keep their margins separate, so these add up.

options.text: One block's `padding-bottom` and the next block's `padding-top`
options.feedback: Padding never collapses; both amounts stay.

options.text: The `margin-right` of one inline-block button and the `margin-left` of the next
options.feedback: Only vertical margins collapse. Horizontal margins always add up.

bricks.hint: Check three things: margin, vertical, normal block flow.
bricks.explanation: Collapsing needs vertical margins touching in normal block flow: siblings, or a parent and its first child with nothing between them.

challenge.prompt: The designer wants 24px of tinted space above this banner's heading. Instead, the gap appears above the banner, outside its background. What's the cleanest fix?

options.text: Give `.banner` `padding-top: 24px` and set the heading's `margin-top` to 0
Give `.banner` `padding-top: 24px` and keep the heading's margin
options.feedback: The padding stops the leak, so the heading's margin now lands inside the banner too: 48px of tint, double what was asked.
It still slips out through the banner's top edge, so you'd get 48px of untinted gap above the banner.
Margin is outside and transparent, and it collapses with the heading's 24px, so the untinted gap stays 24px.

challenge.hint: Which property is painted with the banner's background?
challenge.explanation: The heading's margin escapes because the banner has no top padding or border. Padding is inside the banner, so it's tinted; zeroing the margin keeps the total at 24px.

takeaways: Use padding for space that belongs to the element: inside the border, painted, and clickable.
Use margin for space between elements: outside the border, transparent, and never clickable.
Touching vertical margins in normal flow collapse to the larger one; padding, horizontal margins, and flex or grid items never do.
When a child's top margin leaks out of its parent, move that space into the parent's padding.
